catalog_quote: The language has no contrastive stress, but root-final syllables are prosodically most prominent (§4.2.5). ... 4.2.5. Final-syllable prominence In this section it is argued that final syllables of the phonological word are most prominent in terms of showing the maximal degree of phonological contrasts (§4.2.5.1), they tend to have greater phonetic vowel duration than non-final syllables (§4.2.5.2), and excluding a few exceptional cases, their vowels are the most diachronically stable, which means they are the least likely to be syncopated (§4.2.5.3). ... Stated another way, contrast is greatest at the end of the word, either in the final syllable, or on the final two moras in the case of tone. Maximal contrast is one manifestation of a larger pattern of final-syllable prominence. ... an example like this might make it appear as if the language had rhythmic stress manifested as duration.…

tone_statements.quote: The tone bearing unit (TBU) in Zenzontepec Chatino is the mora, on which there is a three-way tonal specification contrast: High tone (H), Mid tone (M), or no tone ∅ (Campbell 2014, 2016). ... There is a bimoraic minimality preference for lexical forms, which bear one of five basic tone melodies: ∅∅, ∅M, MH, HM, H∅. Monomoraic forms display ∅, M, or H. ... As discussed earlier, Zenzontepec Chatino has a privative tone system, in which a mora may be specified for H tone, M tone or no tone (∅). ... Zenzontepec Chatino has a relatively low tonal density, with about 60% of basic vocabulary bearing no lexical tone (Campbell 2014).

tone_statements.citation: Cruz, Emiliana & Anthony C. Woodbury. 2014. Finding a way into a family of tone languages: The story and methods of the Chatino Language Documentation Project. Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 490-524. hdl:10125/24615
tone_statements.quote: When first approaching tone in Zenzontepec (ZEN) Chatino in 2007, our colleague Eric Campbell found prosodic structures like those in Table 6 ... For monomoraic words, he discovered three tonal options, which he identified as H, M, and no tone (realized as [(M)L] unless affected by spreading or downstep rules which he formulated). For dimoraic words, however, there were seven possibilities, involving seven of the nine logically possible combination of the three options found in monomoraic words. ... It is sufficient to say that the mora is the TBU, and that for each mora, there are three tonal possibilities (aside from the two missing dimoraic patterns, MX and HH).
tone_statements.summary: Two tones, H and M, vs toneless moras (X, default [(M)L]): a three-way choice per mora; 7 of 9 patterns on dimoraic words (Table 8, after Campbell & Carleton). Downstep only mentioned.

tone_statements.citation: Campbell, Eric. 2013. Towards an account of tonal complexity in Zenzontepec Chatino (Otomanguean) verbal inflection. Handout, Society for the Study of the Indigenous Languages of the Americas (SSILA) winter meeting, Boston, MA, 3-6 January 2013. Deposited 2018 in the Chatino Language Documentation Project Dataverse, Texas Data Repository. doi:10.18738/T8/YIRZN9
tone_statements.quote: The TBU in ZEN is the mora. There are two lexical tonal elements: high tone (H) and mid tone (M), but many morae carry no lexical tone (X), yielding a three-way contrast on the mora (H, M, X). Non-compound stems bear one of five common tone patterns (2): 2) X yuu ‘earth’, chaja ‘tortilla’, ... XM keè ‘flower’, ... telà ‘night’, kinì ‘bird’ MH ... lùtí ‘vine’, nkàtá ‘black’, ... HM ... lísù ‘vulture’, ... HX tíi ‘ten’, súkwa ‘six’, ... Stems inflected for 2sg person bear one of two special tone patterns: XH or MM (3) ... The other two possible tone patterns, HH (OCP) and MX, do not occur on single-root stems.
tone_statements.locator: p. 3, §3 'Brief intro to ZEN tone'; last sentence top of p. 4
tone_statements.summary: Two tones H and M vs toneless morae (three-way contrast on the mora); stems carry patterns X, XM, MH, HM, HX; p. 8: 'ZEN has no floating tones at all'. Forms count is a floor (p. 3 only).

tone_statements.quote: Like ZAC, conservative outlier ZEN appears to have SEQUENCES OF TONAL ELEMENTS, but: o There are only two elements {M,H} (alongside toneless elements) ... o Sequence inventory depends on stem mora length: there are seven dimoraic classes (enumerated above) but just three monomoraic classes (X, M, H) ... A. Zenzontepec Chatino (E. Campbell, p.c. 2012), with element inventory {/H/, /M/} but no /L/: • Phonetic [L] is encountered, but can always be derived by a rule • Here, [L] is the default that fills a toneless (X) mora, just as in ZAC ... (19b) ZENZONTEPEC DOWNSTEP: M → L / H __ ... These and similar treatments end up obviating the need to posit an /L/ element for Zenzontepec

tone_statements.summary: Two tonal elements /H/, /M/ plus toneless moras; 7 dimoraic and 3 monomoraic lexical tone-sequence classes on stems; [L] derived (default, or M downstepped after H); no floating tones, spreading yes.

tone_statements.quote: 3. ZEN: Sistema tonal Los elementos tonales (“ tonos ”) ... Asociado a la mora Elemento tonal Notación Realización A(lto) á La mora es alta ascendiente M(edio) ā La mora es media, nivel X (sin tono) a La mora es baja descendiente (por defecto) ... Concluimos que el elemento tonal {A,M} es asociado al mora, no a la sílaba. ... [slide 29 table] Parámetros ZEN ... Niveles fonológicos A, M (nul=B) Contornos no TBU mora Omniprosodicidad fonológico? no Unrestrictedness sí ... Tonos flotantes no Tonía de TBU sin tono Difusión Cambios tonales Downstep
tone_statements.translation: 3. ZEN: Tonal system. The tonal elements ('tones') ... Associated with the mora / Tonal element / Notation / Realization: H(igh) á, the mora is high rising; M(id) ā, the mora is mid, level; X (toneless) a, the mora is low falling (by default) ... We conclude that the tonal element {H,M} is associated with the mora, not the syllable. ... [table] Parameters, ZEN: phonological levels H, M (null = L); contours: no; TBU: mora; phonological omniprosodicity?: no; unrestrictedness: yes ... floating tones: no; pitch of toneless TBUs: spreading; tonal changes: downstep.
tone_statements.locator: slide 17 '3. ZEN: Sistema tonal: Los elementos tonales' (table text); slide 21 'Comparando palabras dimoraicas'; slide 29 '3. ZEN: Resumen de parámetros tonales' (table is an embedded picture, ppt/media/image13.pict)
tone_statements.summary: Two tonal elements H, M on the mora vs toneless moras (default low falling); H spreads to toneless moras and downsteps a following H/M; no contours or floating tones. Analysis credited to Campbell.

tone_statements.quote: (13) ZENZONTEPEC TONE SYSTEM (Campbell 2009) • Domain is the MORA, but combinations restricted within BASE • Small tone inventory o M, H, and X (no tone) (marked with accents over vowels: ā, á, a) o Rising combination: MH o Level combinations: X, XM, HX o Falling combination: HM • H spreads over X (no tone) and downsteps next H or M • No floating tones ... [p. 2 (5)] Tones distributed one per mora in some varieties, one per whole base in others o E.g., for ‘coconut’ ZEN ... (tone to mora), TAT ..., SJQ ... (tone to base) o By either system, 5 (ZEN) to 12 (SJQ) distinct tone patterns for lexical bases

tone_statements.summary: Zenzontepec: per-mora M vs H vs toneless X; base patterns X, XM, HX, MH, HM (5); H spreads over X and downsteps a following H/M; no floating tones. Summary credited to Campbell 2009 (first author).

tone_statements.quote: In Zenzontepec Chatino (Campbell 2014, 2016), the tone bearing unit (TBU) is the mora, and a mora may be specified for high tone (H), mid tone (M), or no tone (Ø). H tone spreads through subsequent toneless moras until it hits another tone or until it reaches the end of the Intonational Unit. H tone causes a subsequent H or M tone to downstep. These features fit the profile of a three-level, privative (Stevick 1969), register tone system (Pike 1948), quite similar to the tone system of the Bantu language Kishambaa (Odden 1982). Bimoraic, morphologically simple words bear one of five basic tone melodies: ØØ, ØM, MH, HM, and HØ. Interestingly, in the play language, the five basic tone melodies are all neutralized as HØ, which is the least frequent of the basic tone melodies in the lexicon (46). Since tone is neutralized, tonal minimal pairs become homophonous in the play language (47). [fn. 13: In trimoraic words, the basic tone melodies align to the final two morae, and the tone of the antepenultimate mora is predictable (Campbell 2016).] ... Play language forms not inflected for 2sg person bear the same tonal melody: (M)HØ. For 2sg pronominal inflection, a single M tone is added t…

Campbell, p.c. 2012), with element inventory {/H/, /M/} but no /L/: • Phonetic [L] is encountered, but can always be derived by a rule • Here, [L] is the default that fills a toneless (X) mora, just as in ZAC ... (19b) ZENZONTEPEC DOWNSTEP: M → L / H __ ... These and similar treatments end up obviating the need to posit an /L/ element for Zenzontepec

tone.translation: 3. ZEN: Tonal system. The tonal elements ('tones') ... Associated with the mora / Tonal element / Notation / Realization: H(igh) á, the mora is high rising; M(id) ā, the mora is mid, level; X (toneless) a, the mora is low falling (by default) ... We conclude that the tonal element {H,M} is associated with the mora, not the syllable. ... [table] Parameters, ZEN: phonological levels H, M (null = L); contours: no; TBU: mora; phonological omniprosodicity?: no; unrestrictedness: yes ... floating tones: no; pitch of toneless TBUs: spreading; tonal changes: downstep.
tone.summary: Two tonal elements H, M on the mora vs toneless moras (default low falling); H spreads to toneless moras and downsteps a following H/M; no contours or floating tones. Analysis credited to Campbell.

sources.quote: (13) ZENZONTEPEC TONE SYSTEM (Campbell 2009) • Domain is the MORA, but combinations restricted within BASE • Small tone inventory o M, H, and X (no tone) (marked with accents over vowels: ā, á, a) o Rising combination: MH o Level combinations: X, XM, HX o Falling combination: HM • H spreads over X (no tone) and downsteps next H or M • No floating tones ... [p. 2 (5)] Tones distributed one per mora in some varieties, one per whole base in others o E.g., for ‘coconut’ ZEN ... (tone to mora), TAT ..., SJQ ... (tone to base) o By either system, 5 (ZEN) to 12 (SJQ) distinct tone patterns for lexical bases
